newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba invites exiles to condemn Helms-Burton law.
newsitem.headline: Cuba invites exiles to condemn Helms-Burton law.

text.p: Cuba was expecting some 150 participants at a conference in Havana this weekend of Cuban authorities and Cuban exiles to discuss opposition to the Helms-Burton law that toughened Washington's longstanding embargo.

Jose Cabanas, in charge of exile affairs at the Foreign Ministry, told reporters on Thursday the two-day conference, starting on Saturday, would include a review of the impact of the law on Cuba and discussions of various legal aspects.

He declined to say who had been invited to the conference, and said only part of it would be open to reporters, noting that for some exiles, discretion was important since participation at such meetings might bring them problems when they returned home.
Cabanas said speakers at the conference would include Economy Minister Jose Luis Rodriguez, Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina and parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon.

Cuba has held two conferences with the exile community since 1994 on the wider theme of drawing closer to the exile community, the majority of whom live in the United States. On both these occasions authorities invited exiles only on condition they held a "respectful" view of the island.

As such, the conferences have been criticised by hardline exile opponents of President Fidel Castro as being gatherings of Cuban authorities and their friends abroad. Authorities have denied this is the case, noting that some participants at past conferences have been critical of Cuba's communist system.

Helms-Burton, approved by President Bill Clinton in 1996, aimed to discourage foreign investment in Cuba and included provisions to punish foreign companies deemed to be benefitting from properties nationalised after Castro's 1959 revolution. It was strongly criticised not just by Cuba but by U.S. allies such as Canada and the European Union.
